prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1058; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened today for a sideswipe that happened while the insured's vehicle was changing lanes. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone to take the initial statement. The account of the lane change matched the description given at first notice.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision and notes the scene conditions without any dispute about how the vehicles came together.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement both line up with the claimant's version of the sideswipe. The contact points on both cars correspond to a side-to-side impact.

Entry 5: Two witnesses gave statements that the claimant's vehicle drifted into the adjacent lane as the other car was passing. Their descriptions agree with each other and with the photos.

Entry 6: Repair estimate came in and the damage pattern on the claimant's vehicle fits the impact described. No prior body damage or unrepaired hits are noted in the inspection.

Entry 7: Confirmed the driver listed on the policy was the person operating the vehicle at the time of loss. Coverage was in force well before the collision, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy.

Entry 8: Medical records received from the claimant's treating provider describe a shoulder injury that is consistent in kind and force with a side impact of this type.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of shoulder injury, and the provider notes ongoing therapy sessions. Reviewing the records further for the reason.

Entry 10: The records show the claimant was treated for the same shoulder area about two years ago. The earlier condition appears to add to the current complaints, and the adjuster is weighing how much of the present treatment relates to this loss.

Entry 11: Spoke with the claimant again to clarify the timeline. The account of the collision and the injury was the same as in every prior conversation, with no changes in the details.

Entry 12: Summary: liability appears clear based on the police report, witness statements, photos, and the other driver's account. Injury evaluation is ongoing, with the prior shoulder treatment and the length of care under review before any settlement discussion.
